title: The Self Through Different Lenses
summary: Nine statements by one fictional person, and seven frameworks for the self applied to all of them. Choosing a framework re-weights the shared evidence board into what is central to it, what it can use indirectly and what it has no concept for; the learner then works out which of four genuine accounts of the same person was written from that framework's premises. After four frameworks a synthesis reports what none of them has been able to make central - including a statement about a fee increase and a cut in hours that six of the seven cannot represent at all.
learningObjectives: Apply seven frameworks for the self to the same body of evidence.
State the question each framework asks and the statements it therefore treats as evidence.
Explain why the frameworks are not competing diagnoses of one person.
Identify what a framework backgrounds, as distinct from what its users believe.
Notice what a vocabulary located inside the person systematically cannot record.
privacy: No data collected, stored or transmitted; the tool asks nothing about the person using it and produces no score for anyone.
accessibilityNotes: Native radios and buttons throughout; no dragging and no timing. The evidence board writes each coding out in words (CENTRAL, usable, no concept) and varies border style as well as tint, so none of the three levels depends on colour; the pinned board is 449px so it stays in view while the seven frameworks and the four candidate accounts are scrolled. Wrong answers produce an explanation of which framework the chosen account actually belongs to and which statements each of the two leans on, never a bare incorrect. Headings do not skip. Changes are announced through the shell's polite live region; reduced motion honoured; forced-colours rules provided; usable at 320px and at classroom-projector widths.
readmeTopic: Seven frameworks for the self applied to one person, and the statement none of them can use
simulationNotes: Nadia and all nine statements are invented for this activity; no real person, interview or case record is reproduced and nothing here is an assessment of anybody. Each framework carries an authored coding for each statement - central, usable or no concept for it - and these codings are teaching judgements that a specialist in any one tradition could reasonably argue with. There is no random generation and no seed; the four candidate accounts for a framework are selected and rotated deterministically so the correct one is not always in the same position. There is no correct lens and no hidden fact about Nadia: what the tool marks is whether the learner matched an account to the framework that generated it. The codings are arranged to make two structural points - that statement 8, about a fee increase and a cut in hours, is marked 'no concept for it' by six of the seven frameworks and central to none, and that statement 9 is coded differently by frameworks that read it as information about Nadia and frameworks that read it as information about the course.
